name: Height subliminals

lead: Height subliminals are audio tracks, often found on video platforms, that people play in the hope of growing taller. They carry affirmations or frequencies below conscious attention and are part of a wider genre of appearance subliminals.

Creators say the masked messages reprogram the subconscious toward growth. Research on subliminal stimuli has found small, context-dependent effects on short-term responses such as thirst-related choices, the American Psychological Association stated in 2009 that there is no conclusive evidence that subliminal stimuli drive behaviour, and no studies of subliminal audio and height were found.

paras: Listeners play the tracks in the background or while sleeping, often nightly over weeks, and many are free on video platforms. They are commonly used alongside other height routines.
The tracks are free audio with no documented physical harms. Listening time and any purchased versions are the main costs.

lead: Height subliminals are audio tracks, often distributed on video platforms, that claim to make listeners taller by playing affirmations or frequencies below conscious attention, typically while sleeping or with music in the background. People use them hoping for added height without surgery or injections; they are free and sit in a wider genre of appearance subliminals that also promises changes such as eye colour.[1]

A Stylist report on the genre describes subliminal videos as often made of ambient music or indistinct speech and notes that one popular channel's most-viewed video was titled 'Grow Taller In 10 Minutes'. It reported searches for subliminal messaging rising by more than 100% in a year and concluded that the evidence that such messages change behaviour is unclear.[1]

Research on subliminal stimuli has found small, context-dependent effects on short-term responses such as thirst-related choices, and the American Psychological Association stated in 2009 that there is no conclusive evidence that subliminal stimuli drive behaviour beyond reinforcing existing tendencies.[2] Studies of audio subliminal self-help tapes have generally found results similar to placebo.[2] No studies were found testing subliminal audio as a way to change height.

paras: Creators describe the tracks as carrying inaudible or masked affirmations meant to reprogram the subconscious mind or growth signalling. Listeners typically play them repeatedly for weeks. Many are sold or given away as downloads, with product pages promising mechanisms such as growth-plate reopening or boosted growth hormone.

Stylist described a surge of subliminal videos on YouTube promising changes from mood to height or eye colour, quoted channel creator Amy Bass saying listeners who feel controlled should not take part in her group, and noted a 2017 petition by more than 740 people claiming a prominent channel hid dark messages.[1] Its overall conclusion was that the jury is still out.[1]

The 1957 claim that flashing words in a film raised soft-drink sales was later admitted by its originator to have been exaggerated.[2] Later laboratory work found small priming effects that appear to depend on the person already having a related need, as in a 2006 study of thirsty participants choosing a primed drink.[2] A study of subliminal words embedded in music found no effect on drink choices, and a trial of 141 undergraduates found subliminal stimulation produced results similar to placebo apart from one self-concept measure.[2] The Stylist article reports the thirst effect lasted under five minutes.[1]
No studies found. Research on subliminal stimuli concerns attitudes, choices and self-concept, not physical growth.

lore.intro: Height subliminals circulate on video platforms and forums, where users post reports of listening for weeks and discuss whether they notice a change.[1]
